$comment: What the Local Static Engine must report for this tree, written by reading
the fixtures rather than by running the engine over them. That distinction
is the point: expectations produced from the engine's own output would only
detect change, never wrongness, and this table is meant to be wrong-able.
Line numbers are in the NEW file, which for a repository commit is also the
line in the fixture as it sits on disk. Severities are the rule's own; what
the threshold does with them is a separate test.

findings.why: A complete SQL literal followed by concatenation.
A template literal with SQL in it and a substitution in it.
The caller chooses the sort column and it is concatenated in.
Concatenation around a quoted value. The apostrophe is inside the double-quoted string, which is the shape the detector missed for two phases.
A SQL literal with a substitution applied by %-formatting.
The same problem spelled as an f-string.
A key-shaped name assigned a string literal.
A password-shaped name assigned a string literal.
An access key ID in the AKIA form. Reported by the AWS rule and not by the generic assignment rule, which is why only one finding is expected on this line.
system runs its argument through a shell.
sprintf does not bound its output.

cleanLines.why: The same query with the value bound, so it can never be parsed as SQL.
The Python driver's placeholder, which is binding by another name.
An assignment whose right-hand side is not a literal.
